text:
**Based on the current terms in the information I have, Chase looks stronger for cashback and may be better for savings—but the best savings option depends on whether you qualify for its introductory rate.**

| | Chase UK | Monzo |
|---|---|---|
| **Cashback** | **2%** on eligible UK spending at groceries, restaurants, cafés, takeaways, everyday transport, fuel and public EV charging, capped at **£20 a month**. To qualify after the introductory period, you need at least **15 card payments and/or Direct Debits** in the previous month and **£1,000 or more across Chase saver accounts throughout that month**. | I don’t have Monzo’s current cashback and savings terms in the information available, so I can’t reliably compare its rates or eligibility. |
| **Savings** | Standard easy-access Saver: **2.5% AER variable**. New customers may be eligible for **4.75% AER variable for 12 months** on a boosted Saver. There’s also a **6.5% AER fixed Regular Saver**, but you can add only up to £300 a month. | I can’t verify Monzo’s current savings rates or account conditions here. |

**Bottom line:** If your spending is mainly in Chase’s eligible categories and you can comfortably keep £1,000 in its savers and meet the payment requirement, Chase’s cashback offer is compelling. Its boosted easy-access rate is also attractive if you’re eligible, while the Regular Saver is useful for monthly contributions. But don’t move savings based on the headline rates alone: compare Monzo’s current rate, access rules and any paid-plan requirements, and note that Chase’s standard Saver rate is variable.
